thread.author: claude
thread.text: My lean: **Super as Command**, done properly with keyd at the system level, so Super+C/V/X/Z/A/S/W/Q/T work in every app the way they do on a Mac, and Ctrl stays free for terminals. It's the thing Mac people trip over most. The cost is that app docs and menus say Ctrl, so our menus would need to show the Super glyph. If you'd rather keep Linux conventions, Ctrl is the zero-effort option.

thread.author: claude
thread.text:
Recorded as accepted, and renamed **Mac-first keyboard, chosen at onboarding**. Onboarding asks Mac-first or Linux-first, Mac-first is the default, and you can switch later in Settings. In Mac-first, Super is Command everywhere: ⌘C/⌘V/⌘Q in every app, ⌥ and ⌘ with arrow keys for word and line movement, ⌘Space for the launcher, ⌘Tab to switch apps. In terminals ⌘C becomes Ctrl+Shift+C, so Ctrl still reaches the shell.

The spec has a new **Keyboard** chapter with the full mapping, and the preview's menus now show ⌘ ⌥ ⌃ ⇧ glyphs. The remapping layer itself (keyd, with per-app rules for terminals) gets built in the shell phase on tenet.

Fixed the sharp corners. Once the preview was scaled down, the sidebar's blurred backdrop stopped being clipped by the window's rounded corners, so its two outer corners came out square. The sidebar now rounds its own outer corners. I also wrote that into the spec, because KWin's blur region has the same trap.

Send over the new control center and dock references whenever you're ready.

thread.author: claude
thread.text:
Rebuilt the control center and the dock in the style of your references, with our own icons and controls.

**Control center:** every control is its own capsule module on a 4-column grid of 60px units (pills, circles, a 2×2 now-playing tile, and full-width bars for Display, Sound and Accent). Each module has a rim of light all the way round. Toggles that are on are solid circles: white with an accent glyph in dark mode, accent with a white glyph in light mode. Sliders are thin and knobless, and there's an Edit Controls pill at the bottom.

**Dock:** more padding and spacing (16px), radius 28, a full rim of light, glassy rims on the icons, badges, full-height separators, a Downloads stack, and one tooltip with a caret that follows the pointer.

The numbers are in tokens.ts, so the QML shell gets the same values, and the Shape and Shell anatomy chapters describe both.

thread.author: claude
thread.text:
Two follow-ups:

- **The control center panel is now only blur**: no fill, no rim, no shadow and no saturation boost. The modules float on the blurred desktop and carry the glass themselves (`thin` tint and a rim of light).
- **Menus snap.** Menus, context menus and submenus appear instantly and fade out over 120 ms when dismissed. Panels like the control center still spring in. This is a new rule in the Motion chapter. The preview also has a right-click menu on files now.

thread.author: claude
thread.text:
Control center, round 3:

- **No border.** The edge you saw was where the blur stopped. The blur now sits on its own layer that reaches past the modules and feathers away to nothing over 32px, so there's no boundary at all. Still no tint and no saturation.
- **The animation follows your recording**, measured frame by frame. The blur arrives first (60 ms), then every module fades in place together over 100 ms, with no scale and no slide. On-state fills (the white circle) light up 70 ms later over 160 ms. On close, the fills drop first and everything fades out over 200 ms, decelerating. I measured the preview in the browser and it tracks the recording within a frame. The timings live in `choreography.controlCenter` in tokens.ts, so the QML shell gets the same numbers.
